summary: The Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme is run by the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust with the University of Oxford. It supports graduates and early career professionals, mainly from low and middle income countries, who hold an offer on one of a limited list of one-year master's-level courses at Oxford. The award pays course fees and a living stipend, and scholars take part in a compulsory Leadership Programme of about 200 hours. Applications go through Oxford, not the Trust.
eligibility_notes:
The programme is for graduates and early career professionals, mainly from low and middle income countries. The Trust's FAQ says the eligible countries and courses are listed on the Oxford website. Stored data (carried over) adds that eligibility is by country of ordinary residence, not nationality, and that refugees and displaced applicants count if their nationality is on the list.

You can apply to the University of Oxford only, and must receive an offer of a place on an eligible course before your scholarship application is considered. The scholarships fund a limited number of 1-year master's-level courses; doctorates (DPhil) are not supported. You must plan to return to your home country or region and work to make a difference in your field. You must also show how the course connects to your career goals and how your work can improve public life in your country.

All courses are taught in English, and you need evidence of English proficiency; you must pass the required English test to be accepted onto the programme. Not open to holders of deferred 2027-28 offers, and (stored data, carried over) current Oxford students are not eligible unless already scholars.

A UK visa brake affects new student visa applications from nationals of some countries (the University lists Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar and Sudan). For courses starting on or after 1 January 2024, family members can join you as student dependants only if you hold a government financial award for study or your course is a Master's by research.

The Trust also runs partner schemes: Chevening (you must be admitted by both the Trust and Chevening, in two separate processes) and a scholarship for Afghan women leaders. Applicants may be considered for more than one scheme.
age_experience_notes: There is no age limit. Work experience is not required, but typical scholars are early career professionals with five or more years of employment experience.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays 100% of course fees, a living-costs stipend (GBP 21,805 in 2026-27) and the cost of a place on the Leadership Programme. It runs for the whole fee liability of the course (9 to 12 months) and the Leadership Programme, which runs from mid-September to early July. Other partners such as Chevening may offer different packages with separate conditions.

requirements.text: Oxford graduate application for an eligible course, submitted by the relevant January (or earlier) deadline for the course, with the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme selected in the University of Oxford Scholarships section. The Trust says not to send your application to the Trust.

Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28, a form from the Oxford scholarship page, submitted at the same time as the graduate application. It should show your motivation, leadership potential and how the course relates to your career and to public life in your country. The Trust's advice page gives no word limit.
Evidence of English proficiency; you must have passed the required English test to be accepted onto the programme. Full requirements are on the Oxford page for your course.
The documents your Oxford course asks for (such as transcripts and references) are part of the Oxford application. They were not readable on the Oxford pages in this pass.

application_steps.title: Choose an eligible course and check country eligibility
application_steps.detail: Applications for postgraduate entry to Oxford open in September. Check that your course and your country of residence are on the Oxford eligibility lists. You can apply only to Oxford, and you must plan to return to your home country or region. MPP applicants are considered for two schemes: the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarship and the Louis Dreyfus-Weidenfeld Scholarship.

application_steps.title: Apply to Oxford and select the scholarship in the application
application_steps.detail: In the University of Oxford Scholarships section of the graduate application, select the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme and upload the Scholarships Statement at the same time, by the relevant January (or earlier) deadline for your course. Do not send the application to the Trust. Deadlines vary by course.

application_steps.title: Oxford decides on your course place first
application_steps.detail: From November to January Oxford assesses applications and each department decides. Only candidates who are offered a place at Oxford can be considered for the scholarship.

application_steps.title: Trust shortlists, interviews online and decides
application_steps.detail: From March to June the Trust contacts candidates and shortlisted candidates have virtual interviews. The panel includes academics from partner colleges and departments, Trust staff and advisers, and alumni. The Trust looks for commitment to developing your country, evidence of change you have already brought about, leadership potential (communication, strategic thinking, enterprise, teamwork), a clear link between the course and your career, and your ability to manage the compulsory Leadership Programme alongside study. Oxford informs successful applicants in May; stored data gives 31 May 2027 for decisions and April 2027 for interviews.

application_steps.title: Prepare for the online interview
application_steps.detail: Interviews test clear motivation for the course, commitment to your country or region, specific evidence of leadership and its impact, and understanding of the Trust. Use a reliable connection, a working camera and a quiet, well-lit space.

application_steps.title: Receive the offer letter in August
application_steps.detail: Successful applicants receive the Oxford scholarship offer letter in August. Participation in the Leadership Programme is written into it and is compulsory. Scholars are transferred to a partner college when they take up the award. Your award letter lists contacts in Student Fees and Funding for questions.

application_steps.title: Attend the introduction in September/October and stay to July
application_steps.detail: Scholars attend a compulsory intensive introduction to the Leadership Programme in Oxford for a few days shortly before the academic year begins. Key events require you to be in Oxford before the September start and to stay until after the official end of Trinity Term in July.
